sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 last closed at 7,183 (Nov 25), about 7% below its 1-month high of 7,744 and in the lower third of its 1-month range of 6,910 to 7,744. The Nasdaq 100 sits at 26,047, roughly 12.6% under its 1-month high of 29,813 and in the lower quarter of its range. The VIX read 26.8 on Nov 26, down from 28.3 the day before, inside a 1-month span of 16.6 to 35.9. The Euro Stoxx 50 is at 6,015, also in the lower part of its 1-month range. The week's earnings load is 35 scheduled reports from S&P 500, Russell 1000 and core names, with 17 of them in technology, mostly software, peaking at 13 on Thursday Dec 3.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Mon Nov 30: ORCL US and NKE US report, with ORCL in the technology group (median -0.08% off recent prints) and NKE in consumer-cyclical (+0.31%). Tue Dec 1: MDB US reports into the same technology group, which is software-heavy this week. Wed Dec 2: SNOW US is the largest software name on the day. Thu Dec 3: DG US reports into consumer-defensive, where the median 3-day reaction is -0.29%. Note that none of this week's reporters sit in the three sectors with the largest recent reactions (mining, copper, energy), and all dates shown are scheduler estimates.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: The largest recent median 3-day reactions are mining at +4.63% across 229 tickers with 2,766 news items (thick coverage), copper at -2.53% across only 6 tickers with 231 news items (a small group, so treat it lightly), and energy at +1.98% across 328 tickers with 5,163 news items (thick coverage). The sectors this week's reporters actually belong to show flat medians: technology -0.08%, consumer-cyclical +0.31%, industrials +0.22%.
